transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to get the wrap disposition plan locked today so we're clear for Friday's set dismantling after the final stage shoot. As we go through this, I need each department lead to confirm the exact disposition and environmental-compliance requirements for your department. If you have any exception to the current draft plan — which sends scenic pieces to a general salvage vendor and places selected hero props in production storage — I need you to state the exact corrective requirement so it can be entered into the meeting record before I can approve. Let's start going through department by department.

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan: the antique jukebox listed as a hero prop is actually a rented piece. I confirmed with the rental house yesterday that its agreement requires it to be returned to the owner in its original condition — it cannot go into production storage or salvage. The exact corrective requirement is to remove the jukebox from the hero props going to production storage and instead schedule its return to the rental house owner in original condition before Friday's set dismantling.

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan regarding environmental compliance. The production's city green-film incentive requires at least 85 percent of dismantled set material by weight to be diverted from landfill. I confirmed with the vendor this morning that the approved vendor's audited plan reaches that threshold only through separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record. However, the compliance packet still contains the general-salvage draft, which does not meet this requirement. The exact corrective requirement is to update the compliance packet and wrap disposition plan to replace the general salvage vendor with the approved audited diversion plan using separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record, ensuring we meet the 85 percent landfill diversion threshold before the plan is locked.
